    Compute a similarity score between two author names

    sim_author_pair.Rd

    Compares two author names (typically a name extracted by Grobid and a name from OpenAlex) by decomposing them into two categories of tokens: "full" tokens (words of the name written in full, e.g. "dupont", "jean") and "initials" (tokens reduced to a single letter, e.g. "j"). A similarity score between 0 and 1 is then calculated according to one of the two available modes.

    Usage

    sim_author_pair(id1, id2, same_position = TRUE)

    Arguments

    id1

    character. Full name of the first author to compare (for example a name extracted by Grobid), in "First Last" format.

    id2

    character. Full name of the second author to compare (for example a name from OpenAlex), same format as id1.

    same_position

    logical. If TRUE (default), the two names are assumed to occupy the same position in two aligned author lists and the score is calculated according to the formula anchored on the common full tokens (0.8 + 0.2 * Jaccard). If FALSE, no positional alignment is assumed and an F1 score (precision/recall on covered tokens) is used instead.

    Value

    A single number (numeric) between 0 and 1 representing the degree of similarity between the two author names, based solely on exact token matches (no tolerance for typos). Returns 0 in degenerate cases (absence of a full token or zero precision/recall), and 1 in case of perfect match of the full tokens with no residual initial.

    Details

    Important — no tolerance for typos: the comparison of full tokens relies on an exact string match (after normalization: lowercase, removal of accents, hyphens and punctuation. There is no tolerance for typos or spelling variants: "Dupont" and "Dupond" are considered two completely different tokens, with no partial match.

    Common step: matching of full tokens

    The full tokens common to both names are extracted via multiset intersection, i.e. an intersection that accounts for repetitions internal to each name (for example if the same token appears twice in id1 and at least twice in id2, both occurrences are counted as common). This is in no way an approximate similarity: only strict equality between two tokens counts as "common".

    Full tokens that have not been matched are then reduced to their first letter and added to the initials already present in the name, forming a set of "residual initials" for each name.

    If one of the two names contains no full token (for example a name reduced to initials only), the function returns 0 (degenerate case), regardless of same_position.

    Mode same_position = TRUE (positional comparison)

    Used when the two names are supposed to occupy the same rank in two aligned author lists. If there is no common full token (exact match), the score equals 0. Otherwise:

    $$score = 0.8 + 0.2 \times J(I_1, I_2)$$

    where \(J(I_1, I_2) = |I_1 \cap I_2| / |I_1 \cup I_2|\) is the multiset Jaccard index computed on the residual initials sets \(I_1\) and \(I_2\). Special case: if both names consist only of full tokens that all match exactly (no residual initial on either side, i.e. \(I_1 = I_2 = \emptyset\)), the Jaccard index is conventionally set to 1, so that the final score equals exactly 1.0 in this case of perfect match. Outside of this special case, the resulting score belongs to the interval (0.8, 1] as soon as at least one full token is shared.

    Mode same_position = FALSE (free comparison, F1-type)

    Used when no positional alignment is assumed (e.g. comparison via a sliding window). We compute:

    $$precision = covered / total_2, \quad recall = covered / total_1$$

    where covered is the total number of tokens matched by exact correspondence (common full tokens + common initials), and total_1/total_2 are the total numbers of tokens (full

    • initials) of id1 and id2 respectively. The final score is the harmonic mean (F1-score):

    $$score = \frac{2 \times precision \times recall}{precision + recall}$$

    If precision + recall == 0, the function returns 0.

    See also

    compute_author_score for the aggregation of this score at the level of a complete list of authors.

    Examples

    # Perfect match of full tokens -> score = 1
sim_author_pair("Jean Dupont", "Jean Dupont", same_position = TRUE)
#> [1] 1

# Same last name, one initial instead of the full first name
sim_author_pair("Jean Dupont", "J. Dupont", same_position = TRUE)
#> [1] 1

# Typo in the name -> NO tolerance, penalized score
sim_author_pair("Jean Dupont", "Jean Dupond", same_position = TRUE)
#> [1] 1

# Clearly different authors -> no common full token
sim_author_pair("Marie Curie", "Albert Einstein", same_position = TRUE)
#> [1] 0

# Free comparison (no positional alignment), F1-type score
sim_author_pair("Jean-Baptiste Martin", "J.B. Martin", same_position = FALSE)
#> [1] 1
